raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

In the Triton split-K (3D) decode path of `kernel_unified_attention`, the 16 segments split the
whole sequence, so with a sliding window only 1-2 segments overlap the window once
`seq_len >> window`, and they walk it serially. This PR splits only the window's tiles into the
segments. Sliding-window decode then costs the same at any context length instead of growing
linearly. Complementary to #60418, which routes RDNA sliding-window layers to TRITON_ATTN;
interacts with #56148 (multi-query split-K), see Details.

## Claims

- **Per sliding-window layer, decode on TRITON_ATTN:** the cost no longer grows with context.
  1.57× faster at 4K, 2.73× at 8K, 3.90× at 12K and ~10× at ≥ 32K tokens (window 2048, batch 1,
  cold L2; AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700).
- **End to end, Muse Glimmer 30B, TP=4 on 4× R9700, `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`:**
  - TPOT −1.2% at 4K and **−4.9% at 12K** context (c=1);
  - unchanged below the window;
  - GSM8K unchanged.
- **gpt-oss-20b** (window 128, attention sinks; TP=1 on one R9700): correct with sinks;
  sliding-window attention per call 10.3 → 5.0 µs in serving (rocprofv3); TPOT −0.1…−0.3% at
  c=1. The gain is smaller because the window spans only 8-9 tiles.
- **No change where the window does not bound the keys or the path differs:**
  - full attention, context ≤ window (~1% overhead there, see Details);
  - the 2D path, spec-decode verify (`max_seqlen_q > 1`);
  - chunked-local, multimodal-prefix, R-SWA and per-sequence-causal masks.
- **Tests:** two new tests guard that the window layout is actually used and is correct; the
  existing numerical test would not notice it silently turning off.

## Validation

**Kernel microbenchmark.** Setup: R9700 (gfx1201), 8 q / 1 KV heads, head 128, block 16, bf16,
window 2048, batch 1. Statistic: rocprofv3 kernel-duration median of 100 dispatches per case,
CUDA-graph replay, baseline (`window_aware_segments=False`) and change interleaved in one process,
L2 flushed (512 MB) before every call. Values are `kernel_unified_attention` + `reduce_segments`:

| context | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 760 – 2K | 7.0–12.5 µs | 7.1–12.6 µs | 0.99–1.00× |
| 4K | 19.5 µs | 12.4 µs | 1.57× |
| 8K | 33.5 µs | 12.3 µs | 2.73× |
| 12K | 48.0 µs | 12.3 µs | 3.90× |
| 32K – 128K | 122 µs | 12.2 µs | 10.0× |

The new cost equals a full-attention layer over 2048 keys, i.e. the work of the window spread over
16 segments.

<details>
<summary>Batch sizes 4 / 16 and hot-L2 results</summary>

Speedup (before / after), window 2048:

| context | bs 4 cold | bs 16 cold | bs 1 hot | bs 4 hot | bs 16 hot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4K | 1.16× | 1.02× | 1.70× | 1.63× | 1.15× |
| 8K | 1.92× | 0.98× | 2.61× | 2.85× | 1.75× |
| 12K | 2.64× | 0.99× | 4.48× | 4.11× | 2.45× |
| 32K | 6.10× | 1.88× | 11.3× | 10.6× | 5.89× |

Full-attention control (identical kernel under both labels): ratio 1.000 median.

Below the window, three repeated hot runs with 300 dispatches each give 0.978–0.998× on SWA
layers (window-range arithmetic) and 0.998–1.003× on full layers.
</details>

**End to end.** Muse Glimmer 30B, TP=4 on 4× R9700, TRITON_ATTN, best stock config, 3 interleaved
rounds, round-to-round spread ≤ 0.02 ms at c=1. Measured on the first revision of this change
(identical kernel logic, before the test/helper commit), ported onto vLLM `98dff2a81`:

| workload | TPOT before → after | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| multimodal 512 → 128, c=1 (under the window) | 27.18 → 27.13 ms | 33.94 → 34.00 |
| text 4K → 512, c=1 | 27.95 → 27.60 ms (−1.2%) | 33.16 → 33.55 |
| text 12K → 512, c=1 | 29.42 → 27.99 ms (−4.9%) | 27.70 → 28.85 |

**gpt-oss-20b** (window 128, attention sinks; TP=1 on one R9700, default TRITON_ATTN), 3
interleaved rounds, random 2K/8K/16K → 256 tokens, `--max-num-seqs 16`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT c=1, 2K / 8K / 16K | 27.03 / 27.31 / 27.69 ms | 26.99 / 27.22 / 27.61 ms (−0.1 … −0.3%) |
| SWA attention per call in serving (rocprofv3, 8K, c=4) | 10.34 µs | 4.96 µs |
| full attention per call in serving | 129.8 µs | 129.7 µs |

The gain is small here because the 128-token window spans only 8-9 tiles and attention is a
minor part of the MoE step. At c=4, end-to-end TPOT varied by ±4-10% between rounds with the
prefill/decode schedule, far above the expected ~0.1%. The kernel trace above is the reliable
measure, and decode-only steps were not slower (58.47 → 57.67 ms median).

Greedy outputs are deterministic per variant and diverge only at near-ties (top-2 probabilities
within 0.02).

GSM8K 25-shot for Muse Glimmer (prompts 3.3K-4.9K tokens, all beyond the window): flexible-extract
0.9363 → 0.9348, strict-match 0.9371 → 0.9356 (± 0.0067); 99.2% identical answers.

**Correctness and tests (gfx1201):**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_triton_attn_segments.py \
       tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py \
       tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py \
       tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py
```

- 2244 passed. One failure, `test_triton_unified_attention_per_token_head_scale[int4-16-128-num_heads0-seq_lens1]`,
  fails identically on unmodified `main` on gfx1201 (int4 KV path, which does not reach this code).
- After the final commit, `test_triton_unified_attention.py` + `test_triton_attn_segments.py`:
  1970 passed.
- Differential check, new vs old split vs fp32 reference: GQA 1/5/8, windows 8/16/17/64/2048, with
  and without attention sinks, contexts at every window/tile edge. Error vs fp32 is unchanged;
  new vs old differ by ≤ 0.5 bf16 ulp.
- The new tests were checked by seeding bugs:

  | seeded bug | `test_window_aware_segments_gate` | `test_split_k_window_segment_tile_ranges` | numerical test |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | gate silently off | fails | – | passes |
  | `reduce_segments` without the flag | fails | – | fails |
  | wrong active-segment count | – | fails | passes |
  | window start off by one tile | – | fails | fails |

**CI.** The tests live in `tests/kernels/attention`, which runs in the Buildkite kernel shards
(NVIDIA and MI300). RDNA (gfx1201) is not in CI; the results above were collected locally.

## Details

**Root cause.** `tiles_per_segment = cdiv(seq_len, NUM_SEGMENTS * TILE_SIZE)` lays the segments
over `[0, seq_len)`. `compute_tile_loop_bounds` then intersects each segment with the window. For
`seq_len >> window` the window falls into one or two segments, each walking up to
`min(window, seq_len / 16)` tokens serially, while the other segments exit. The cost therefore
grows with context until `seq_len = 16 × window`.

**Change.**

- `split_k_segment_layout()` (new, `triton_attention_helpers.py`) returns
  `(base_tile, tiles_per_segment, num_active)`. With `WINDOW_SEGMENTS` the segments cover the
  decode query's window tiles `[⌊max(L−W,0)/T⌋, ⌈L/T⌉)`; otherwise the whole sequence, with the
  same values as before. Both `kernel_unified_attention` and `reduce_segments` call it, so they
  always agree on which segments are active.
- `compute_tile_loop_bounds()` gets an optional `segm_base_tile_or_0` (default 0); other callers
  are unchanged. The kernel's early exit becomes `segm_idx >= num_active`, which is equivalent to
  the previous condition.
- The launcher enables `WINDOW_SEGMENTS` only for the 3D path with `max_seqlen_q == 1`, causal,
  and a plain sliding window: not chunked-local, mm-prefix, R-SWA or per-sequence causal. In
  those cases the window does not bound the keys of a single decode query, or (spec-decode
  verify, enabled in 3D by #56148) there are several queries per sequence. Both kernels receive
  the same flag. `reduce_segments` gets `SLIDING_WINDOW` only when the flag is on, to avoid
  compiling a reduce variant per window size.
- `window_aware_segments: bool = True` on `unified_attention()` forces the old split. The new
  tests and the A/B benchmark use it.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- About 1% slower on SWA layers when the context is shorter than the window: the window-range
  arithmetic runs even when the window covers everything (≈ 0.05 µs of ~5 µs).
- No benefit:
  - for multimodal-prefix models with an image in the batch (`mm_prefix_range` is batch-wide);
  - for the int4 per-token-head KV cache (separate kernel);
  - above the 3D threshold (`128 / KV heads per GPU`);
  - on backends other than TRITON_ATTN.
- On ROCm, plain-SWA models default to ROCM_ATTN unless TRITON_ATTN is selected (or #60418
  applies). Models with sinks (gpt-oss) and mm-prefix models already land on TRITON_ATTN.
- No CPU/GPU synchronization is added: the gate uses only host-side launcher arguments.
- Complexity: +82 / −9 lines outside tests.

---

+@triton.jit
+def _split_k_tile_ranges(
+    output_ptr,
+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    SLIDING_WINDOW: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    WINDOW_SEGMENTS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    seq_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    segm_idx = tl.program_id(1)
+    seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + seq_idx)
+    base_tile, tiles_per_segment, num_active = split_k_segment_layout(
+        seq_len, 16, SLIDING_WINDOW, TILE_SIZE, WINDOW_SEGMENTS
+    )
+    # One decode query at position seq_len - 1, as in kernel_unified_attention.
+    loop_lo, loop_hi, _ = compute_tile_loop_bounds(
+        seq_len - 1,  # context_len
+        seq_len,
+        1,  # cur_batch_query_len
+        0,  # q_block_local_idx
+        segm_idx,
+        tiles_per_segment,
+        TILE_SIZE,
+        16,  # BLOCK_M
+        2,  # BLOCK_Q
+        8,  # num_queries_per_kv
+        SLIDING_WINDOW,
+        False,  # USE_MM_PREFIX
+        True,  # IS_3D
+        segm_base_tile_or_0=base_tile,
+    )
+    out = output_ptr + (seq_idx * 16 + segm_idx) * 3
+    tl.store(out, loop_lo)
+    tl.store(out + 1, loop_hi)
+    tl.store(out + 2, num_active)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "sliding_window,tile_size,window_segments,seq_lens",
+    [
+        (2048, 16, True, [1, 100, 2047, 2048, 2049, 4096, 4103, 33000, 131072]),
+        # All 16 segments active.
+        (1024, 32, True, [4096, 131072]),
+        # 17 window tiles: 2 per segment, only 9 segments active.
+        (257, 16, True, [1040]),
+        # Windows that are not / are a multiple of the tile size.
+        (17, 16, True, [1, 16, 17, 18, 1000]),
+        (16, 16, True, [16, 17, 33]),
+        # Window inside a single tile.
+        (8, 32, True, [1, 5000]),
+        # Without window segments the whole sequence is split, as before.
+        (0, 16, False, [1, 1000, 4103]),
+    ],
+)
+def test_split_k_window_segment_tile_ranges(
+    sliding_window, tile_size, window_segments, seq_lens
+) -> None:
+    """Active split-K segments walk disjoint, consecutive slices of the
+    window's tiles that cover it exactly, at most cdiv(window_tiles, 16)
+    tiles each; inactive segments walk nothing."""
+    num_segments = 16
+    seq_lens_t = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    ranges = torch.empty(
+        (len(seq_lens), num_segments, 3), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE_TYPE
+    )
+    _split_k_tile_ranges[(len(seq_lens), num_segments)](
+        ranges,
+        seq_lens_t,
+        SLIDING_WINDOW=sliding_window,
+        TILE_SIZE=tile_size,
+        WINDOW_SEGMENTS=window_segments,
+    )
+    for seq_len, seq_ranges in zip(seq_lens, ranges.tolist()):
+        end_tile = -(-seq_len // tile_size)
+        first_tile = 0
+        if window_segments:
+            first_tile = max(seq_len - sliding_window, 0) // tile_size
+        num_tiles = end_tile - first_tile
+        per_segment = -(-num_tiles // num_segments)
+        num_active = -(-num_tiles // per_segment)
+        if not window_segments:
+            assert per_segment == -(-seq_len // (num_segments * tile_size))
+        for segm_idx, (lo, hi, active) in enumerate(seq_ranges):
+            assert active == num_active
+            if segm_idx < num_active:
+                assert lo < hi
+                assert (lo, hi) == (
+                    first_tile + segm_idx * per_segment,
+                    min(first_tile + (segm_idx + 1) * per_segment, end_tile),
+                )
+            else:
+                assert hi <= lo
